title: Lying to a Judge: The DOJ Penalty

scenes.title: Hook — Above the Law?
scenes.narrationSummary: Most people think government lawyers can lie without consequence, but a Rhode Island judge just demanded a DOJ attorney personally face sanctions.

scenes.title: Surface — Personal Summons
scenes.narrationSummary: A federal judge ordered a DOJ lawyer to show cause why he shouldn't be sanctioned for misstating facts, a rarely used personal penalty.

scenes.title: Hidden Mechanism
scenes.narrationSummary: The hidden three-layer mechanism includes a personal response under oath, a bar referral, and an internal DOJ investigation, putting the lawyer's career at risk.

scenes.title: Sanction Statistics
scenes.narrationSummary: Federal judges sanction prosecutors in fewer than 0.5% of cases, but when they do, it can end careers, as shown by a recent California reprimand.

scenes.title: Tradeoffs of Accountability
scenes.narrationSummary: The accountability mechanism works only when misrepresentation is clear-cut and the judge is willing, failing when the government quickly backtracks or for policy officials.

scenes.title: Payoff — Rhode Island Is Different
scenes.narrationSummary: The Rhode Island judge rejected the usual soft exit, personally ordering evidence, signaling the court is ready to pierce institutional shields, and one lawyer may face personal justice.
